newsitem.title: USA: CME committee looks for Nov start to OSB contract.
newsitem.headline: CME committee looks for Nov start to OSB contract.

text.p: The Forest Products Committee of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange is looking for a November start to its new Oriented Strand Board (OSB) contract, pending Board approval.

OSB, a wood panel product similar to plywood, is used in roofing, flooring and sheathing a house, and will complement the CME's existing futures and options on two-by-four Random Length lumber, a CME marketing announcement said.
The contract would be traded in the lumber pit and calls for on-track delivery of 100,000 square feet of 7/16-inch OSB.
The new contract was approved for trading by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on September 27.
The Forest Products Committee will now submit the contract to the Agricultural Oversight Committee and then on to the Board of Directors for final approval on a start up date.

The contract, for Chicago delivery, would be quoted in dollars per 1,000 square feet, with a minimum price fluctuation (tick) of $0.10, equalling $10 per contract. Contract months would be January, March, May, July, September and November. Maximum daily price limits of $10.00 would be expanded to $15.00 after two consecutive daily limit moves. Trading hours would mirror lumber, 0900 to 1305 CDT (1400 to 1805 GMT).

Trade sources said the new contract differs from the CBOT contract. CME's contract is based on OSB product only instead of an index which included both OSB and plywood. CME's contract is also settled by physical delivery whereas CBOT's contract was cash settled.
